problem:
Find the coefficient of $(x-5)^{2}$ in the second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\sqrt{x+4}$ at $x=5.$ Do not round the answer.

The coefficient of $(x-5)^{2}$ is
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
The second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=5$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =f(5)+{f}^{′}(5)(x-5)+\frac{{f}^{″}(5)}{2}(x-5)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient of $(x-5)^{2}$ in the above Taylor polynomial is

$$
\frac{{f}^{″}(5)}{2}.
$$

To find this coefficient, we start by computing the second derivative ${f}^{″}(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\sqrt{x+4}=(x+4)^{1/2} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{2}(x+4)^{-1/2} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\frac{1}{4}(x+4)^{-3/2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate ${f}^{″}(x)$ at $x=5.$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(5)=-\frac{1}{4}(5+4)^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{4}\cdot {9}^{-3/2}=-\frac{1}{108}.
$$

Finally, we determine the coefficient of $(x-5)^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{″}(5)}{2}=\frac{(-\frac{1}{108})}{2}=-\frac{1}{216}\end{aligned}
$$
